q: As we go from left to right across the Periodic Table, the elements change in properties from metals to ____.
e: As we go from left to right across the Periodic Table, the elements change in properties from metals to non-metals. Non-metals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These elements except Al are called ____.
e: These elements except Al are called metalloids. Metalloids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrogen is also a ____.
e: Hydrogen is also a non-metal. Non-metal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Electronegativity is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of ____.
e: Electronegativity is a measure of the tendency of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons. An electron is a tiny negative particle that occupies shells around the nucleus.

q: In the Periodic Table, in general, electronegativity of elements increases from left to right across a period, and from the bottom of a group to the ____.
e: In the Periodic Table, in general, electronegativity of elements increases from left to right across a period, and from the bottom of a group to the top. Top is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Atoms with high electronegativity tend to form ____ ions.
e: Atoms with high electronegativity tend to form negative ions. Negative is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Atoms with low electronegativity, which is highly electropositive elements tend to form ____ ions.
e: Atoms with low electronegativity, which is highly electropositive elements tend to form positive ions. Positive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The most electronegative element is ____.
e: The most electronegative element is fluorine. Fluorine is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The least electronegative (most electropositive) element is ____.
e: The least electronegative (most electropositive) element is caesium. Caesium is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The noble gases or inert gases are neither electropositive nor ____.
e: The noble gases or inert gases are neither electropositive nor electronegative. Electronegative is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Atomic radii decrease from left to right across a ____.
e: Atomic radii decrease from left to right across a period. Period is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This is because ongoing from left to right across a period, the nuclear charge increases while the added electrons enter the ____ shell.
e: This is because ongoing from left to right across a period, the nuclear charge increases while the added electrons enter the outermost shell. Outermost is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The increased nuclear charge attracts the electrons in the outermost shell closer to the nucleus, hence the shell ____ resulting in smaller atoms.
e: The increased nuclear charge attracts the electrons in the outermost shell closer to the nucleus, hence the shell contracts resulting in smaller atoms. Contracts is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The atomic radii increase from top to bottom down a group in the Periodic ____.
e: The atomic radii increase from top to bottom down a group in the Periodic Table. The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number so similar properties sit in groups.

q: This is because as the number of electrons increases, these additional electrons are in the larger electron shells making them farther and farther from the ____.
e: This is because as the number of electrons increases, these additional electrons are in the larger electron shells making them farther and farther from the nucleus. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell.

q: When one or more electrons are removed from a metal atom, a positive ion or ____ is formed.
e: When one or more electrons are removed from a metal atom, a positive ion or cation is formed. Cation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thus, a positive ion is always ____ than its parent atoms.
e: Thus, a positive ion is always smaller than its parent atoms. Smaller is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When one or more electrons are added to a neutral atom, a negative ion or ____ is formed.
e: When one or more electrons are added to a neutral atom, a negative ion or anion is formed. Anion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thus, a negative ion is always ____ than its parent atom.
e: Thus, a negative ion is always larger than its parent atom. Larger is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The amount of energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom to form a gaseous ion is called the ____ energy.
e: The amount of energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom to form a gaseous ion is called the ionisation energy. Ionisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In general, ionisation energies increase from left to right across a ____.
e: In general, ionisation energies increase from left to right across a period. Period is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In general, ionisation energies decrease down a ____.
e: In general, ionisation energies decrease down a group. Group is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The noble gases have the highest ____ energies.
e: The noble gases have the highest ionisation energies. Ionisation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The electron affinity of an element is the energy released when an electron is added to a gaseous atom to form a gaseous ____.
e: The electron affinity of an element is the energy released when an electron is added to a gaseous atom to form a gaseous ion. Ion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The electron affinities generally increase from left to right across a ____.
e: The electron affinities generally increase from left to right across a period. Period is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The electron affinity decreases on moving down a ____.
e: The electron affinity decreases on moving down a group. Group is the idea that completes this fact.
